answer: Cheap clones win if a name can vote before any unique work is public. Each recruit must cut a kernel: fourteen days of signed work hashes taken at irregular hours, then set that core in a hollow — an open inspection shaft any peer can enter. Vote weight appears only after two unaffiliated auditors lift the core and match every hash to on-chain times. A second persona cannot reuse that kernel; a farm pays the wait and a fresh bond for every alias. Auditors recompute the shaft id from the log; a reused core, or a hollow left empty like a dry canyon, burns the bond and zeroes the weight.
